title: Kingdom of Seisyllwg
capsule: Seisyllwg was a Welsh petty kingdom of the southwestern central coast, formed when Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi were combined, traditionally under the dynasty of Seisyll ap Clydog who gave his name to the realm. After its last native king Gwgon ap Meurig drowned around 872 leaving no heir, the kingdom passed by marriage to the line of Rhodri Mawr of Gwynedd, whose grandson Hywel Dda came to rule it. In the early tenth century Hywel united Seisyllwg with neighbouring Dyfed to create the enlarged kingdom of Deheubarth, a consolidation effectively complete by about 920, after which Seisyllwg ceased to exist as a distinct realm.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Seisyllwg's two constituent regions (Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi) are geographically defined; the kingdom's territorial extent relative to neighboring Welsh polities is reasonably attested in medieval Welsh annals, though exact boundaries are conventional approximations.
